items.title: Show HN: Minigraf – An embedded, bi-temporal graph database in Rust
items.contentSnippet:
A successor project to my previous attempt at building a temporal graph database (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=23455516). This one builds on its predecessor's concept, but drops the dependency on another database to provide the storage, transaction and query engines. Minigraf is self-contained, packaged as a library crate, embeds into your application, and supports full bi-temporality.

items.title: Show HN: EarWing, an open source hardware device for transcription
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN!
I've been shocked by the amount of money people are paying for hardware transcription devices and subscriptions for the software.
I built EarWing, which you can 3D print and assemble yourself. It uses a ESP32 dev board and 4 microphones for noise cancellation and has a browser offload for transcription and summary generation (using LLMs running in the browser).

items.contentSnippet:

The problem is that AI writing is VERY easy to spot and most of the time I don't want it being sent under my name, since it does not sound like me at all.

items.title: Show HN: Word Legion: Clash Royale-like where any spellable word becomes a troop
items.contentSnippet:
What if Clash Royale had an infinite deck?
That was the idea, inspired by some other NLP-based games. Instead of picking troops, you spell them from a rack of letters. The meaning of the word sets what the unit does: SNAKE poisons, GHOST goes invisible, DRAGON flies and burns.
Power comes only from length, rare letters and how rare the word is, so long weird words hit hard. Every word you play goes into your collection, which lives on a little farm, in a Stardew Vally fashion, bc why not ahah
